doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Parties, weddings, balls and Sunday work schedule
summary: Laine describes the occasions that hired bands and his punishing Sunday schedule from Milneburg to the parks across the river.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Can you tell us all the different occasions that would hire music when you were young? You once told me they used to have weddings and everything else. They'd always hire a band. What kind of parties? Yes.
Parties and band, weddings and stuff like that. Yes. Parties. I played a many, many long party. I, with top pollin spread out there, up in the Irish Channel. With top pollin spread over the mud.
I played a many of them.
What do you think? I taught him, Mr. Russell. You met Mr. Russell?
I think one time you were talking with Chink Martin and you said that almost every wedding they'd always have a band in those days. Yes. Yes.
Almost every wedding. It was surprise parties. King parties. King parties. King K cutting outfits. So on and so on. Yes, it had music. This one had to do with your, uh,
Yeah. Oh no, that's all right.

Give you a little breeze. Oh! I have the mic pointed the other way. I don't think it'll pick up the sand. Uh, what other kind of parties did you play? Any other kind of special parties or anything else?

No, nothing but balls. The balls were the balls of course and picnics. Yes. Sure. But parties like that. Weddings and surprise parties and something like that. You know. How many nights a week did you work? Well, I'll tell you. Some weeks I'd be going putting air every night. Putting air every night. I'd be playing. Yeah. Every night. Every night. Even when I'd play at Millenburg. I'd play at Millenburg. I'd play at Millenburg. We'd start at Millenburg playing out there at nine o'clock in the morning. Understand on a Sunday. On Sunday. On Sunday. And after we'd play Millenburg, I had to go over the river with the bands and get them all to play parks, different parks over the river. See? After we got done playing at Millenburg. See? And we'd go over the river and play them parks. Look. I would play the parks up until twelve o'clock. Sometime extra hours over. One or two hours over. See? We'd play that. You know. Extra hours. See? And we'd play that. And I'll never forget as many days as I live. Those bands that organized after I organized color bands. They'd play in these camps almost close to one another. They'd say, you better play music. There are Lions Banders over there. Jack Lane's Banders over there. You probably better play good music. You say that to one another, you know. There was a nigga by the name of Green. He's dead. He used to tell me a whole lot of this stuff, too. He used to tell me a whole lot. None of the stuff they played, they used to copy off me. He said that. None of the stuff they played, they'd copy it off of my band. He used to tell them, you better play music. Jack Lane is over here to a line.
